vulnerability_analysis: The contract maintains two total supply variables: _tTotal (used for reflection calculations) and _tTotalSupply (returned by totalSupply()). In _takeLiquidity(), when burn fees are applied, burnAmount is subtracted from _tTotalSupply but _tTotal remains unchanged. This creates a discrepancy where the reflection ratio (rTotal/tTotal) becomes distorted. As owner, we can set high burn fees, then perform transfers to trigger fee collection, reducing _tTotalSupply while keeping _tTotal the same. This makes the reflection rate (rTotal/tTotal) increase, meaning each token represents more reflection value. By then transferring tokens to excluded addresses or manipulating the system, we can extract value.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to gain control. 2. Set high burn fees (e.g., 100% of liquidity fee). 3. Acquire some KARMA tokens. 4. Perform transfers to trigger fee collection and burn tokens, reducing _tTotalSupply. 5. Exploit the distorted reflection ratio to increase our token balance. 6. Convert tokens to ETH via the DEX pair.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call setBuyFeePercentages/setSellFeePercentages to set high burn fees. 3. Use deal() to give ourselves initial KARMA tokens. 4. Perform transfers between addresses to trigger fee collection and burn tokens. 5. Check that our balance increases due to the reflection ratio distortion. 6. Optionally swap tokens for ETH to realize profit.
